summary: Buck Peak lookout, Klamath County, OR: built 1932, staffed at least into 1960, burned and removed November 1968. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 21-foot tower with a model L-4A 14x14 cab and hip roof
facts.status_note: Removed by burning in November 1968; no source describes what remains

events.note: Forest Service proposal July 1932; Interior approval September 3, 1932; tower 21 feet per two sources, 10 feet per register
Operated under Rogue River National Forest, Lake of the Woods district; Columbia Utilities Company provided telephone
Lightning struck the tower while the lookout was eating; the lightning started a fire that grew to about an acre and a half
Jack and Lorraine Holmes with their daughter, 1950-1953
Lookout reported smoke from a fire in logging slash; held at about half an acre

Disposed of by burning in November 1968; October 30, 1968 memo from Winema forest supervisor set the burn; R.D.M.A. personnel did the burn; a November 13, 1968 memo said it would incur no cost to the project; register gives removal 1968

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives a 10-foot wooden L-4 tower and a camp from 1915; WillhiteWeb and Forest Lookouts give a 21-foot tower with an L-4A cab after the 1932 plans. The story uses the 21-foot account, which two sources share, and notes the register's version. Not reconciled, so height_m is left out of facts.

notes_for_editor: Read: the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register page, WillhiteWeb's 1932-1968 history, and the Forest Lookouts Oregon page with dated memos and newspaper items. Removal in November 1968 is well supported by two sources. Height conflict is unresolved (10 ft in the register, 21 ft in the other two). The register's 1915 camp is not in the other sources. Both secondary sites name Crater National Forest as the 1932 builder; not checked and not used. No source describes condition, access or visitor status today. Worth trying: Winema National Forest records for the 1968 burn, Klamath County newspapers 1932-1968, and the original clippings behind the Forest Lookouts page (for example the 1963 Herald and News item).
